name: Linear Diophantine systems via Smith Normal Form

source.question: Can the parametric solution extend to systems of linear Diophantine equations (matrix form Ax = b over ℤ), characterizing the full solution lattice via the Smith Normal Form?

knowledge.progressSummary: COMPLETED: Built Smith Normal Form infrastructure in Lean 4. Defined SmithNormalForm structure with unimodular matrices, diagonal form, and invariant factor chain. Axiomatized SNF existence and solvability criterion. Proved bezout_from_snf (classical Bézout recovery), null space ℤ-submodule structure, and affine lattice characterization of solution sets. 2 axioms, 1 sorry, 11 proved theorems.
builtItems: IsUnimodular predicate with closure properties (identity, product)
SmithNormalForm m n structure with U, D, V, divisibility chain
intNullSpace with ℤ-submodule closure (zero, add, smul)
Gallery entry with meta.json, annotations.json, index.ts
insights: Mathlib has no Smith Normal Form for PIDs/ℤ — transvection machinery targets fields only
mulVec_add, mulVec_sub, mulVec_smul are the key linearity lemmas for null space proofs
IsUnimodular closure under product follows from det_mul and natAbs_mul
Solution lattice structure proof is clean: forward uses mulVec_sub + sub_self, backward uses ← mulVec_sub + sub_eq_zero
Divisibility chain for SNF should use ℕ index (not Fin m × Fin n) for clean bounds
mathlibGaps: No Smith Normal Form in Mathlib — only transvection diagonalization for fields
No invariant factors or elementary divisor theory for PIDs
